title: Synthetic SLO drift autopilot: cohort replay + autoresolve dashboard
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: We currently detect SLO regressions reactively via production golden-signal alerts. This leaves a blindspot for gradual SLO drift caused by model or infra changes (small p95/p99 shifts, KV-prefetch regressions, or tenant-specific tail-latency). We need a deterministic, replayable way to surface and (optionally) temporarily auto-remediate SLO drift before customers see impact.

Goal: Build a dashboard and automation pipeline that 1) continuously replays synthetic cohort traffic across regions and priority paths, 2) computes cohort-level SLO deltas (token-level p50/p95/p99 and decode vs prefetch breakdown), 3) visualizes drift and root-candidate signals, and 4) wires an "autoresolve" canary that can briefly lower load (soft shed) or rollback route weighting when a reproducible regression is confirmed.

Scope / acceptance criteria: 
- Instrumentation: add new metrics tags: pipeline_stage (prefetch|decode|postprocess), cohort_id, region, tenant_bucket, route_version. Each metric value must be exported as labeled histogram/timing for token-latency and a boolean for kv_hit.
- Synthetic replay harness: a scheduler that issues deterministic, parameterized requests (cohorts) to a shadow route in each region with failure injection controls. Runs every 5m by default.
- Dashboard: panels for cohort p50/p95/p99 token-latency trends, decode vs prefetch contribution stacked area, kv_hit ratio over time, synthetic burn-rate and repro-rate, per-cohort deviation score (0-100), and timeline of circuit/callbacks when autoresolve triggers.
- Autoresolve: experimental flag gated; when enabled, reproducible regression (>=3 consecutive replays with p99 increase > 30% and repro-rate > 90%) creates a temporary route rollback or reduces route weight by configurable percentage for 10m, with automatic re-evaluation. All actions must be auditable in the runbook log.
- Telemetry: ensure synthetic requests are tagged and excluded from customer billing; synthetic traces must propagate tenant_bucket and cohort_id.
- Runbook & alerts: add escalation steps and define SLO burn thresholds that map to PagerDuty.

Design notes & trade-offs: 
- Why synthetic cohorts? Production probes are noisy; dedicated cohorts make drift signals reproducible. But risk: synthetic traffic can miss rare production patterns. Mitigation: include sampled real-traffic shadow replays for high-volume tenants.
- Autoresolve risks: automated rollback could mask real incidents if the regression is downstream or data-dependent. We require high repro-rate and region-consistent signals before any change; autoresolve is opt-in per-customer. All changes are reversible and logged.
- Metric cardinality: adding pipeline_stage and cohort_id increases cardinality. We will keep cohort_id to a bounded set (max 25 active cohorts) and use cardinality-aware aggregators for rollup storage.

Implementation plan: 
1) Instrumentation (2s): add pipeline_stage tagging in runtime's token timing emitter and kv_hit boolean. Update Prometheus/telemetry producer to export histogram buckets matching existing token buckets.
2) Replay harness (2s): implement a lightweight scheduler service that reads cohort definitions from config and posts to the shadow route with tracing headers. Include chaos toggles for artificial tail latency and KV miss injection.
3) Dashboard & scoring (2s): build Grafana dashboard with panels and a computed "cohort deviation score" that weights p99 drift and repro-rate. Implement a simple scoring lambda for real-time computation.
4) Autoresolve & runbook (2s): implement control-plane action that can adjust route weights/rollbacks with an approval flow and audit log. Gate behind feature flag.

Rollout plan: 
- Stage 1: internal-only cohorts + dashboard in staging. Run for 2 weeks to tune scoring and bucket sizes.
- Stage 2: opt-in customers and internal SRE teams. Enable autoresolve in a dark mode that logs decisions but does not act.
- Stage 3: controlled autoresolve for low-risk routes (non-production tenants), progressively broaden.

Open questions / next steps: 
- Cohort selection: propose default cohort sets (short-chat, long-chat, single-turn instruction, embeddings batch). Need PM and Research to approve canonical payloads.
- Storage for high-cardinality histograms: propose moving cohort rollups to a TSDB with rollup support (Mimir/Thanos + preaggregation). Ops to evaluate cost.
- KPIs: false positive rate of autoresolve, detection lead time vs production alerts, and cardinality cost.

Related artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SLO/ENG-903999+Synthetic+SLO+Autopilot (draft), Design diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/file/d/1abcdXYZ-slo-harness, Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8123

Notes for reviewers: focus on metric labels and the safety criteria for autoresolve. If you think 3 replays at 5m windows is too permissive, suggest thresholds.

Acceptance tests: 
- Synthetic replay reproduces a known injected 40% p99 slowdown in staging and the dashboard shows deviation score > 70.
- Autoresolve in dark mode logs the correct rollback decision but does not change traffic.
- Metrics emitted have correct tags and are excluded from billing pipeline.
